column1: CX - Define MVP Error Taxonomy and Logging Rules
column33:
Define the minimum error categories and naming conventions required to standardize the Login flow. Establish conventions for {{error.key}}, {{correlation.id}}, HTTP status mapping, log severity, and safe handling of sensitive information. The taxonomy must distinguish expected authentication failures from unexpected backend or dependency failures. Avoid building a complete catalog for unrelated modules.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* The Confluence page defines the required error response fields and the naming convention for {{error.key}}.

* Expected authentication failures and unexpected server/dependency failures have documented categories and HTTP status mappings.

* The conventions for {{correlation.id}} and log severity are documented, including generation and propagation expectations.

* The document specifies sensitive fields that must never appear in client responses or logs, including passwords, access tokens, and secrets.

* The MVP taxonomy and unresolved design decisions are ready for review before implementation begins.

*Deliverable*

Approved Confluence document defining error categories, naming conventions, HTTP status mapping, correlation ID rules, and sensitive-data policies.

column1: CX - Assess Dependency Criticality for Login
column33:
Analyze the dependencies involved in Login and determine how their failure could affect authentication. Classify each relevant dependency by runtime necessity, impact of failure, and whether Login can continue when the dependency is unavailable. Use code inspection and existing behavior as evidence; do not infer criticality solely from business familiarity or configuration presence.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* Each dependency confirmed to participate in Login has a documented criticality rating: {{Critical}}, {{High}}, {{Medium}}, or {{Low}}. Explanation of each criticality here: [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/crx/pages/617512964|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/crx/pages/617512964|smart-link]

* The rating includes a short rationale covering the impact of failure on Login and whether the flow can continue or degrade gracefully.

* Unknown behavior is explicitly marked as {{Needs validation}} rather than presented as a confirmed fact.

* The criticality assessment is added to the Confluence inventory and reviewed with the backend owner.

*Deliverable*

Completed dependency criticality matrix with ratings, impact rationale, and unresolved validation items.

* -Users who have completed onboarding are not shown the onboarding flow again based on the updated validation logic.-
* -The Android onboarding behavior is consistent with the existing iOS onboarding validation behavior.-

column1: TD - Add Comparison button
column33:
Implement a new *Comparison date* toggle button on the dashboard so users can compare the currently selected date range against the immediately preceding equivalent period. The dashboard currently supports date range filters for 30d, 90d, and all time; this task adds comparison support for 7d, 30d, and 90d ranges while disabling comparison for all time.

When the toggle is active, the selected range should determine the comparison window: 7d compares against the previous 7 days for a total 14-day window, 30d compares against the previous 30 days for a total 60-day window, and 90d compares against the previous 90 days for a total 180-day window. The active toggle state must be reflected in the URL using a query parameter and handled through Next.js SSR so the comparison state is preserved on page load. Count cards should display updated improvement values based on the comparison data.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* -The dashboard displays a new *Comparison date* toggle button with active and inactive states.-
* -The toggle is enabled only for supported date filters: 7d, 30d, and 90d; when the selected filter is all time, the toggle is disabled.-
* -When active with the 7d filter, the dashboard compares the selected 7-day range against the previous 7 days and calculates comparison values using a total 14-day data window.-
* -When active with the 30d or 90d filter, the dashboard compares against the previous equivalent period, using a total 60-day window for 30d and a total 180-day window for 90d.-
* -When the toggle is active, the comparison state is added to the URL as a query parameter, handled through Next.js SSR, and the count cards display the updated improvement values from the comparison data.-

column1: CX - Review the bug related to the onboarding variable on Android and iOS.
column33:
The error became evident because an account was created from scratch in creditorX on an iOS device; when it was created the onboarding process finished and in the database the variable was set to 1 and the login worked correctly. It was also tested on Android showing that the login is performed correctly. After some time it stopped working and the following scenarios occurred:

* When entering on iOS it requested phone number verification, but if the same user logged in on Android that did not happen — there the normal flow could continue. If you check the database the variable verify_phone is always 1, that is, as if it were already verified. First problem: why does one device request it and the other not.
* To solve the previous point the onboarding was changed to 0, so on iOS it allows continuing the process without issue, but now when logging in on Android it redirected to the first login. The error is that on Android and iOS there are different behaviors when changing the onboarding field, which should not be the case.

Description Review the Case Track documentation and repository to understand the project's purpose, technologies, architecture, and overall functionality.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -Understand the project's main objectives and use cases.-

h3. Questions and General Findings

{quote}* *URL:* [https://casetrack.com/login/|https://casetrack.com/login/]
* According with the documentation, this project has Dev and Stage environment, but URLs are not working. 
* We need test accounts and .env, maybe AWS.
* How accounts are created and the account creation workflow
* Are there the tests updated?{quote}

h3. Case Track — Brief Investigation

{quote}*Purpose:* Case Track provides Cordoba’s legal team with a focused workspace for *settlement offer reviews and lawsuits*. It complements Forth CRM rather than replacing it. [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RD/pages/107905045/Overview|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RD/pages/107905045/Overview|smart-link]

*Technologies:* The documented stack includes *React, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, and AWS*, with GitHub Actions for deployment. [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RD/pages/31752193/Project+Architecture+Overview|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RD/pages/31752193/Project+Architecture+Overview|smart-link]

*Architecture and functionality:* Forth supplies client, debt, and case information through synchronization. Case Track maintains local records and adds user management, role-based access, assignments, tasks, notes, and legal workflows. Webhook endpoints receive notifications containing record IDs, suggesting subsequent requests to retrieve details from Forth. [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RD/pages/109183021/Cases|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RD/pages/109183021/Cases|smart-link] · [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RD/pages/35520513/API+Documentation|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RD/pages/35520513/API+Documentation|smart-link]{quote}



h3. *Difficult Tasks* 

Doing a brief researched conducted, since my point of view, this tasks could be difficult: 

{quote}*#3 — Historical Forth offers not showing (Difficult)* Right now the app only knows how to update an offer it already has — there's no way for it to go back and pull in old offers from Forth for a debt. We'd need to build that "fetch all past offers" piece, plus a way to backfill the ones we're missing today.

*#4a — "PROD RSAPI" name showing instead of real user (depends)* Do Case Track Accounts have Forth Account ID? 

*#4b — Recently viewed files (Difficult)* This doesn't exist at all yet. There's no tracking of "who looked at which file and when," so we'd need to add a new table for that, record a view every time someone opens a file, and build a new screen/endpoint to show the list. It's a real new feature.

*#7 — Create settlement offers in-app (Difficult)* Offers are only ever created in Forth today — this app just receives them afterward. To let users create offers directly here, we'd need a whole new piece: a form/screen, the backend logic to save it, and a way to push it over to Forth. We also haven't confirmed Forth even has an endpoint to accept a new offer from outside their system — that's something we need to verify with them before we can commit to a timeline, since it affects whether this is a backend build or a bigger conversation with Forth.{quote}



h3. *Current Deploy Flow*

{quote}* Push to {{development}} → deploys to *dev*
* Push to {{main}} → deploys to *qa* (not production!)
* Push to {{release-candidate/**}} → deploys to *staging*
* Pushing a tag {{v*.*.*}} → deploys to *prod* (this is the real production trigger)

So even though {{development}} is GitHub's "default" branch, it's not special in the pipeline — {{main}} triggers a deploy just the same, just to a different environment (dev vs qa){quote}

column1: CP - BACK - Auth - Testing onboarding reset endpoint is exposed in production
column33:
h2. Description

{{POST /api/v1/auth/onboarding/reset}} was added as a testing endpoint (the code is marked "remove this endpoint after testing is completed"), but it is still deployed to every environment, including production.

The endpoint is anonymous and takes only an email. For the matching user it clears the password, marks onboarding as not completed, and removes the Terms/Privacy acceptance and the onboarding access token. In production, anyone who knows a client's email can lock that client out of their account with a single request. The different responses for unknown and known emails also reveal which emails have a portal account.

It can't be used to take over an account, because completing onboarding again requires the code sent to the client's email. The endpoint is still useful for resetting test accounts in local, dev and stage, so it should stay available there.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* In production, the endpoint doesn't exist (it returns 404 and doesn't show up in Swagger).
* In local, dev and stage, the endpoint keeps working as it does today.
* The endpoint is enabled only in an explicit list of environments, so an unrecognized or missing environment keeps it disabled.
* Production logs are reviewed for any past calls to this endpoint, and the result is noted on the ticket.
* The Android app is checked so it doesn't call this endpoint in production builds.

column1: CP - BACK - Forgot Password - Users whose email changed in Forth can't recover their account
column33:
h2. Description

When a client's email is changed directly in Forth, the portal's local user keeps the old email until the next successful login. Login already handles this: it resolves the account through Forth by email, then by Contact ID, and syncs the new email after the password is verified.

Forgot Password doesn't go through Forth. It looks the user up only by the locally stored email. A user who changed their email in Forth and then forgot their password can't recover access through the normal flow; today the only way out is an undocumented workaround or contacting support.

HED-1594, HED-1938 and HED-1973 moved Login and Onboarding to resolve users by their Forth identity. This ticket closes the remaining known gap in the changed-email scenario: Login, Onboarding and Forgot Password should all handle it, so the user can regain access from the portal on their own, without needing to contact support.

column1: CP - WEB - Onboarding - Rebuild Step Guard And Progress Stepper
column33:
h2. *Description*

Stems from [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1849.|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1849.|smart-link]. 

Onboarding's step guard never ran: its trigger, {{OnboardingStepper}}, had been commented out since the repo's first commit, and OnboardingProvider was never mounted. The logic had also gone stale, so it couldn't simply be reconnected. Users could open any onboarding step via URL; it only failed on submit, when the backend rejected the onboarding access token. The visual stepper was dead code for the same reason.

This ticket rebuilds the guard as a reusable hook with no UI dependency (to be reused by [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-2006|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-2006|smart-link]) adds onboarding's rules on top of it, and rebuilds the stepper as its own presentational component.

h2. *Initial Findings*

* OnboardingStepper is purely presentational — the redirect logic lived entirely in OnboardingProvider.
* The old guard encoded the pre-[HED-1595|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1595?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiMjI4NGI3MzkwMTQyNDc2ZGJmOTc2MzI0Mjc3YmNiNTciLCJwIjoiaiJ9] step order, and no live screen wrote its completion flags — reconnected as-is, it would have redirected every user on every step.
* The old provider's step-data helper stored form values, including the password, in localStorage.
* Landing on an unprotected step didn't bypass real access control — the backend's onboarding access token already blocked an invalid submission. This was a UX/consistency gap, not a security hole.

h2. *Acceptance Criteria*

* -Opening Agreement, NewPassword, or Verify without a valid onboarding access token (missing or expired) redirects to Login with a "session no longer active" message.-
* -Opening a step after passing OTP but skipping a previous one redirects to the first incomplete step.-
* -Opening OTP without having submitted the email redirects to Start.-
* -Once onboarding is finished, earlier steps lead to the Completed screen.-
* -Normal step-by-step onboarding is unaffected, and every attempt runs the full flow starting at Agreement.-
* -Progress from an earlier or abandoned attempt never carries over, and leaving onboarding (back to-
* -Login, finishing, or an expired session) clears its stored state.-
* -Every onboarding step except Completed shows its position in a visual progress indicator, in English and Spanish.-
* -The guard has no dependency on the stepper or any UI, so other flows can reuse it.-
* -In local dev, a URL parameter lets a developer open any step directly; it has no effect in production builds.-

h2. *Deliverables*

* Reusable step-guard hook with a dev-only bypass, ready for HED-2006.
* Onboarding step rules driven by a single ordered step list shared with the stepper.
* Visual progress stepper on every onboarding step except Completed.

*PR:* [https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-frontend/pull/322|https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-frontend/pull/322|smart-link] 

*PR Notes*

h2. Summary
Onboarding's step guard never ran: its trigger ({{OnboardingStepper}}) had been commented out since the repo's first commit, and {{OnboardingProvider}} was never mounted. The logic had also gone stale (pre-HED-1595 step order, no screen writing its completion flags), so reconnecting it as-is would have redirected every user on every step. Its step-data helper also stored form values, including the password, in localStorage. Users could open any onboarding step by URL; the backend only rejected them on submit.
This PR replaces it with a reusable, UI-free step-guard hook, adds onboarding rules on top of it, and rebuilds the stepper as a presentational component.
h2. Technical notes
* *Generic guard:* {{useStepGuard({ isAllowed, redirectTo, onRedirect })}} has no UI dependency, so HED-2006 can reuse it on the Login and Forgot-password OTP screens. In dev only, {{?skipGuard}} opens any step directly ({{import.meta.env.DEV}}, absent from the production bundle).
* *Single step list:* {{onboardingFlow}} defines the order once. The guard and the stepper both derive from it.
* *Rules:* if onboarding is finished, every step redirects to Completed. Steps after OTP require a valid onboarding access token, otherwise the user goes to Login with a "session no longer active" message. Otherwise the user goes to the first incomplete step.
* *State:* progress is stored as completed-step ids only (no form data). The token expiry from the OTP response is stored and checked by the guard. {{OnboardingProvider}} and {{onboardingStorage}} were removed.
* *Exit cleanup:* a single routine clears onboarding state on every way out (back to Login, finishing, expired session, guard redirect).
* *Login no longer clears onboarding state on mount.* That approach was tried and dropped: react-admin remounts the app on a language change and syncs the locale across tabs, so a second tab on Login wiped an onboarding in progress. The token-expiry check covers the stale-session case instead.
* Every attempt runs the full flow (Agreement is never skipped), so web doesn't use the backend's {{onboardingStatus}}.
* Completed doesn't require the token, so reloading it after the token expires still shows success.
* The OTP step now uses the onboarding {{Layout}}, like the other steps.

*Root cause:*
The guard's trigger was commented out and its provider never mounted since the initial migration into this repository; the logic itself had also gone stale (pre-HED-1595 step order, no screen writing its completion state).

*Approach:*
A generic, UI-free step-guard hook, plus onboarding rules driven by one ordered step list that both the stepper and the guard derive from. Progress is stored as per-attempt completion flags only (no form data). The onboarding access token's expiry is stored and checked by the guard. A single exit routine clears onboarding state on every way out (back to Login, finishing, expired session, guard redirect to Login). The stepper was rebuilt as a presentational component, and the OTP step now uses the same onboarding layout as the other steps.

*Decision:*

* The guard is separate from the stepper so HED-2006 can reuse it on screens without a stepper.
* Clearing onboarding state when Login mounts was tried and dropped: react-admin remounts the app on language change and syncs the locale across tabs, so a second tab on Login wiped an onboarding in progress. Replaced by explicit exit points plus the token-expiry check.
* Every attempt runs the full flow (Agreement is never skipped), so web doesn't use the backend's onboardingStatus.
* Completed doesn't require the token, so reloading it after the token expires still shows success.

*1. Full flow*

* Setup: Start → OTP → Agreement → NewPassword → Verify → Completed, checking localStorage at each step.
* Expected: the stepper advances on every step; completedSteps grows to ["start","otp","agreement","newPassword","verifyIdentity"]; clicking Login on Completed clears all onboarding keys.

column1: CP - BACK - Auth - Add Rate Limiting to Onboarding Start Endpoint
column33:
h2. Description

{{POST /api/v1/auth/onboarding/start}} is anonymous and takes only an email. Each request searches Forth and, for a client without a portal account, creates the local user and emails them a verification code.

Today the endpoint is protected only by the IP-based limit added in HED-893 (5 req/s, shared by every auth route). That's about 18,000 requests per hour from a single IP, with no limit when the IPs rotate. As a result:

* any client's inbox can be flooded with codes they never requested;
* every request uses up the shared Forth quota, which login and onboarding also depend on;
* emails can be probed at high volume.

[https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-893|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-893|smart-link] already noted that limiting by user requires an application-level layer. This ticket adds that layer for the endpoint, and a stricter IP limit at the Ingress.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Repeated requests to onboarding start for the same email are rejected with 429 after 3 attempts in 15 minutes, before any Forth search or email is sent.
* The limit response is identical whether or not the email exists.
* The same per-email limit applies to password reset.
* Onboarding start has its own IP limit of 10 requests per minute without bursts above that, and the rest of the auth routes keep their current limit.
* Rate-limited requests return 429 in dev, stage and prod, and the 429 setting is versioned in the repository.
* Web and iOS show the existing "too many requests" message, with no client changes.
* Normal onboarding and password reset work as before for a real user.

column1: CP - Document login and onboarding account-resolution flows in Confluence
column33:
*Login (SignInAsync)*

* 0 Forth matches → {{InvalidCredentials}}
* 2+ Forth matches, no local account → {{InvalidCredentials}}
* 2+ Forth matches, local account exists → *resyncs that account via its own ContactId first*, then normal login against it _(antes decía "no Forth resync that attempt" — ya no es así, se corrigió)_
* 1 Forth match, no local account at all → {{InvalidCredentials}} (no more auto-redirect to onboarding)
* 1 Forth match, local account exists, onboarding not finished → {{InvalidCredentials}} *— login no longer resumes onboarding at all; resuming is only possible via* {{/ob-start}} _(antes decía "OnboardingRequiredVia2FA (resume, unchanged)" — ese comportamiento se eliminó por completo)_
* 1 Forth match, local account exists, onboarding finished → normal login (password/2FA as usual)

*Onboarding Start (StartOnboardingAsync)* — sin cambios, sigue exactamente como lo tenías:

* 0 Forth matches → {{CustomerNotFound}}; if a local account still has that exact email (stale), opportunistically resynced against its own Forth data first
* 2+ Forth matches → {{MultipleCustomersFound}}, blocked
* 1 Forth match, no local account for that contact, email free locally → creates account, sends OTP
* 1 Forth match, no local account for that contact, email claimed by a different local account → resyncs that other account first; still claimed after → {{EmailAlreadyRegistered}}; freed up → creates account normally
* 1 Forth match, local account exists for that contact, already onboarded → syncs that account, then {{AlreadyOnboarded}}
* 1 Forth match, local account exists for that contact, not yet onboarded → syncs, continues, sends new OTP (resume)



h2. Technical notes

*Login (*{{SignInAsync}}*)*

Before:

* Forth search returns null (truly zero results) → {{InvalidCredentials}}
* Forth search returns a contact (whether it was the only match or just the first of several) → resyncs the local account found by that contact's ContactId, then logs in
* No local account exists for that ContactId → {{OnboardingRequiredVia2FA}} (auto-redirected into onboarding, regardless of password)
* Local account exists but onboarding not finished → {{OnboardingRequiredVia2FA}}
* Local account exists and onboarding finished → normal login

After:

* 0 Forth matches → {{InvalidCredentials}}
* 2+ Forth matches, no local account → {{InvalidCredentials}}
* 2+ Forth matches, local account exists → resolves the candidate by the local account's own ContactId (not by whichever contact Forth happened to list first), resyncs, then tries to log in
* 1 Forth match, no local account at all → {{InvalidCredentials}}
* 1 Forth match, local account exists, onboarding not finished → {{InvalidCredentials}}
* 1 Forth match, local account exists, onboarding finished → normal login

*Onboarding Start (*{{StartOnboardingAsync}}*)*

Before:

* Local account found by raw email text match → used directly; Forth is never consulted at all, regardless of how many Forth matches would've existed
** already onboarded → {{AlreadyOnboarded}}, returned before any Forth call
** not yet onboarded → resends OTP using the stale local data as-is, no Forth call, no sync
* No local account found by raw email text → only now is Forth consulted
** Forth returns nothing → {{CustomerNotFound}}
** Forth returns a contact, no local account for that ContactId, email free locally → creates account, sends OTP
** Forth returns a contact, no local account for that ContactId, email already claimed by a different local account → {{CreateCustomerUserAsync}}'s {{CreateAsync}} result is never checked; creation would fail Identity's uniqueness validation, but the code proceeds as if it succeeded, sending an OTP tied to a user that was never actually persisted

After:

* 0 Forth matches → {{CustomerNotFound}}; a stale local account with that exact email gets opportunistically resynced
* 2+ Forth matches → {{MultipleCustomersFound}}, blocked, no account created
* 1 Forth match, no local account, email free → creates account, sends OTP (unchanged)
* 1 Forth match, no local account, email claimed by a different local account → resyncs that other account first;
** still claimed → {{EmailAlreadyRegistered}}
** freed up → creates account normally
* 1 Forth match, local account exists, already onboarded → syncs first, then checks — local record stays current even when blocked (*before:* never synced in this branch at all)
* 1 Forth match, local account exists, not yet onboarded → syncs, continues, sends new OTP (*improvement, not unchanged:* the old code never called Forth or synced in this branch — this is a net-new benefit worth calling out, not parity)

column1: CP - WEB - SPIKE - Review step-guarding across multi-step auth flows
column33:
*Description*

Multi-step flows (login OTP, forgot-password, onboarding, profile updates) rely on client-side checks to stop users from landing on an intermediate step without completing the previous one. Coverage looks inconsistent: while reviewing HED-1828, we found forgot-password's OTP step has no such guard (unlike its own next step), the same gap exists in login's OTP screen, and onboarding's guard logic exists but is disconnected — the component that triggers it is commented out.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -Inventory of each multi-step flow and whether it guards against direct/skipped-step access.-
* -Root cause for the disconnected onboarding guard.-
* -A recommended, consistent pattern to guard steps.-
* -Call on whether the fix should be one ticket or split per flow.-

*Deliverables*

*Inventory:*

||Flow||Guard present?||Mechanism||
|Onboarding intermediate steps (Agreement/NewPassword/Verify/Completed)|Exists but never runs, and is stale|OnboardingProvider.validatePreviousStepCompletion is never triggered: <OnboardingStepper /> is commented out in onboarding/Layout.tsx and OnboardingProvider is never mounted. The logic also encodes the step order from before [HED-1595|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1595?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNTlmNjI1MGRkNjNkNGVlZTk4MzViZDY1NzcyZWE3YjIiLCJwIjoiaiJ9], and no live screen writes the completion flags it reads.|
|Login OTP|None|Reads MFA info on mount but never validates/redirects on it.|
|Forgot-password OTP|None|Same pattern as Login OTP.|
|Forgot-password "set new password" (post-OTP)|Working|Checks the OTP-verification result passed via router state and redirects back if missing. The only guard in the codebase that currently works.|

Onboarding intermediate steps (Agreement/NewPassword/Verify/Completed) | Exists but never runs, and is stale | 

*Root cause:*

Onboarding: the guard was never wired up — its trigger component has been commented out since the initial migration into this repository, unnoticed because a later backend check still blocks an invalid submission, just with a worse error. It has also gone stale: it encodes the step order from before [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1595|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1595|smart-link] (NewPassword → Verify → Agreement; today it's Agreement → NewPassword → Verify), and no current screen writes the completion flags it reads. Reconnected as-is, it would redirect every user on every step, so it has to be rewritten, not reconnected.

Generically: the one existing guard is hardcoded against onboarding's own step enum, routes, and storage — not parameterized — so it could never have been reused by the other flows even if someone had tried. No shared step-guard utility exists anywhere in the codebase today.

*Recommended pattern:*

A single reusable guard hook (current step, required step, fallback route, and state source as parameters), fully decoupled from any UI — usable by flows with no visual step indicator (Login OTP, Forgot-password) as well as by onboarding, which pairs it with its own separate, purely presentational stepper component instead of bundling the two together. 

Include a dev-only bypass as part of the same shared hook — gated by both a build-time dev check and an explicit opt-in query parameter — so a developer can open any step directly for UI work without disabling the guard during normal local navigation, and with no footprint in production builds.

*Scope decision:*

Two tickets.

Ticket 1 — [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-2005?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNmEyZTEwN2QwOWY3NDc1N2FiZTIwZDBlOTY2OTc0NjAiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-2005?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNmEyZTEwN2QwOWY3NDc1N2FiZTIwZDBlOTY2OTc0NjAiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link] (priority, build now): Build the new shared guard hook, decoupled from any UI, plus the dev bypass. Reconnect onboarding's visual stepper (dead code, commented out since the repo's first commit) as a standalone presentational component, paired with the new hook instead of the old hardcoded OnboardingProvider validation logic. Priority: now — the missing visual progress indicator is the actual driver, and since the guard has to be rebuilt as part of that same work anyway, it ships working instead of left disconnected again.

Ticket 2 — [https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-2006?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiN2NkYTJmZGEyOWVkNDJhY2E0MmM1ZmIyNWMzNTI4ZGIiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-2006?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiN2NkYTJmZGEyOWVkNDJhY2E0MmM1ZmIyNWMzNTI4ZGIiLCJwIjoiaiJ9|smart-link] (follow-up, created now, scheduled later): Wire the shared hook built in Ticket 1 into Login OTP and Forgot-password OTP, neither of which has any guard today, and migrate Forgot-password's existing working guard (currently its own inline location.state check) onto the same shared pattern for consistency. Priority: lower — both screens already fail safely without a prior step, since the backend rejects the OTP attempt regardless, so this is a consistency cleanup, not an active gap.

column1: CP - WEB - Inconsistent and non-localized date formats across the app
column33:
*Description*

Dates are displayed inconsistently across the app, using several different formats, and in most cases without respecting the user's selected app language. 

* Profile shows "User Since" as {{MM/DD/YYYY}}
* The Onboarding identity verification step shows the date of birth as {{MM.DD.YYYY}}
* The Graduated card shows a long, localized format (e.g. "May 7, 2026" / "7 de mayo de 2026"). 

This creates a visually inconsistent experience and, since {{MM/DD/YYYY}} is ambiguous outside the US, can lead to misreading dates for non-US users.

*Initial Findings*

* A shared, locale-aware formatter ({{formatLocalizedLongDate}}) already exists but is used in only 2 of ~17 places where dates are shown (Graduated card, Dashboard next payment).
* Everywhere else — Profile, Onboarding DOB, Notifications, Debts (Settlement/Lawsuit), Learning Center, Documents & Statements, Transactions — builds dates independently, mostly hardcoded to {{MM/DD/YYYY}} regardless of app language.
* The statement month filter hardcodes English month names with no translation.
* Table/list row dates (Documents, Transactions) are reasonably dense as {{MM/DD/YYYY}}, but not locale-aware.
* Month-grouping headers correctly show only month + year, but two different mechanisms are used — one follows the app's language, the other ({{toLocaleString('default', ...)}}) follows the browser's.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* Month and day names reflect the app's currently selected language (English/Spanish) wherever the format is written out (e.g. "May" / "mayo"), not a hardcoded or browser-default locale.
* Dates representing a single specific day shown as a primary/standalone value (Profile "User Since", Graduated date, Dashboard next payment, Settlement due date, Lawsuit court date) are displayed in long form (e.g. "May 7, 2026" / "7 de mayo de 2026").
* Dates shown in dense table/list rows or as secondary metadata (Documents, Transactions — including mobile views, Settlement line items, Notifications, Learning Center video "date added", Onboarding date of birth) are displayed in a numeric day/month/year format using a single fixed order, independent of the app's selected language.
* Dates used only to group or filter by month (table month headers, statement month filter) show only month and year, with the month name translated and capitalized consistently in both languages.
* The Onboarding date of birth field no longer uses a dot-separated format; it follows the same fixed numeric order used elsewhere in the app.
* A date-only value (no time component) displays as the correct calendar day regardless of the viewer's timezone.
* A missing or invalid date value renders as "-" instead of breaking the page.
* No regression in how dates are parsed or submitted to the API — only display formatting changes.

h2. *Deliverables*

PR: [https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-frontend/pull/323|https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-frontend/pull/323|smart-link] 

*PR Notes*

h2. Summary
Dates were shown in inconsistent formats across the app and mostly ignored the selected language. All date display now goes through a shared {{dateFormatters}} module:
* *Long localized* for standalone dates (Profile "User Since", Graduated, Dashboard next payment, Settlement due date, Lawsuit court date).
* *Numeric MM/DD/YYYY* (fixed order, per the updated AC) for table rows and metadata (Documents, Transactions, Settlement items, Notifications, video date added, date of birth).
* *Translated month/year* for grouping headers and the statement month filter.
Moving from {{dayjs}} to {{Intl}} exposed that date-only values ({{Date}} scalar) parsed with {{new Date()}} display one day early in timezones behind UTC. Parsing is now centralized in the formatters with {{parseISO}}, which reads them as local dates.
h2. Technical notes
* Invalid dates render {{-}} instead of throwing.
* No changes to how dates are sent to the API.
* Also included: Transactions mobile showed the raw {{processDate}}; Spanish lawsuit labels fixed ({{Fecha de Corte}} → {{Fecha de audiencia}}, {{N.º de caso}}, {{Citación judicial}}).

column1: CP - Enable and validate OTP/email delivery ahead of production launch
column33:
*Description*

As part of production launch preparation, the OTP bypass that had been in place for development and testing purposes needs to be disabled, and transactional email/OTP delivery needs to be re-enabled and verified end-to-end.

While preparing this, it was identified that email delivery is currently blocked at the SendGrid account level, which would prevent OTP and other transactional emails (forgot password, email verification, etc.) from reaching users once the bypass is removed.

*Initial Findings*

* A direct request to SendGrid's API ({{POST /v3/mail/send}}) using the current API key returned an IP Access Management error: {{"The requestor's IP Address is not whitelisted"}}.

!image-20261005-151741.png|width=619,alt="image-20261005-151741.png"!

* This indicates the SendGrid account has IP Access Management enabled, restricting which outbound IPs are allowed to authenticate — this applies at the account/API key level, so it affects both direct API calls and the backend's SMTP relay (MailKit) used to send OTP and other transactional emails.
* Each environment (dev/stage/prod) egresses through a single NAT Gateway with its own static Elastic IP. The outbound Elastic IPs for each environment have been identified:
** Prod: {{54.157.239.52}}
** Stage: {{54.208.186.38}}
** Dev: {{52.0.63.118}}
* SMS-based OTP delivery via BlueRock was verified and confirmed working — tested directly against BlueRock's API (Postman), and end-to-end by temporarily enabling real OTP sending ({{Mfa:SendEnabled = true}}) both locally and in the production environment. The issue is isolated to the email channel (SendGrid) and does not affect SMS delivery.

!image-20261005-160120.png|width=684,alt="image-20261005-160120.png"!

!image-20261005-160137.png|width=684,alt="image-20261005-160137.png"!

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -The OTP bypass used for development/testing purposes is disabled for production.-
* -The production environment's outbound IP (NAT Gateway) is whitelisted in SendGrid's IP Access Management.-
* -Transactional emails (OTP, forgot password) are successfully delivered end-to-end from the production environment.-
* -Login, forgot password, and email-verification OTP flows are confirmed working with real email delivery.-

*Blocked By*

Whitelisting the production IP in SendGrid's IP Access Management requires access to the SendGrid account, which this team does not currently have. The identified IPs above were shared with Guillermo, who forwarded them to John (account owner) to add them to the allowlist.

*Decision*

The OTP bypass was temporarily re-enabled in production (Mfa:SendEnabled = false) on 2026-10-05 to avoid blocking other production launch preparation work while the SendGrid IP whitelist request is pending with John. It will be disabled again once email/OTP delivery is confirmed working end-to-end.

column33:
h2. Description

CreditorX Android and iOS customers are currently seeing a generic *“Error”* message when attempting to log in with valid credentials. This message does not explain the root cause or provide enough information to reproduce or diagnose the problem.

Previous research by [~accountid:712020:f5e366c6-65b6-45ab-af69-01a539ce9b27] indicates that the generic error appears when the Kazoo login flow fails. The issue only occurs when the customer’s login credentials are valid. When credentials are invalid, the client correctly returns the message *“User not found or incorrect”*.

Additional investigation is needed to identify why Kazoo fails during valid login attempts, improve observability around the failure, and return a clearer error message to the customer when this scenario occurs.

[~accountid:712020:f5e366c6-65b6-45ab-af69-01a539ce9b27] also noted that, during each login attempt, the system changes the password in Kazoo because the Kazoo user password is required to authenticate against the Kazoo API. Since Kazoo does not provide an endpoint to retrieve the current password, the system creates a new password during each login attempt to know the active password.

!!!!But saying it's because of Kazoo is just a guess; with this error message, it's impossible to determine if Kazoo is the cause. Part of this task is figuring out what's causing the login to fail.

!image-20261005-195050.png|width=203,alt="image-20261005-195050.png"!

* -The backend logs enough diagnostic information to identify when a valid login fails because of a Kazoo authentication or password update issue.-

+After a customer logs+ in to the iOS app, display an in-app popup inviting them to rate and review the app using the native App Store in-app review flow. The experience should open the App Store rating and review modal inside the app, without redirecting the customer to the App Store app.

The popup should appear at an appropriate moment immediately after login, avoid interrupting critical user actions, and gracefully handle cases where the App Store review flow is unavailable or dismissed by the customer.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* -Given a customer successfully logs in to the iOS app, when the post-login experience loads, then the app shows a popup inviting the customer to rate and review the app.-

* -Given the customer chooses to leave a rating or review, when the popup action is selected, then the native App Store in-app review modal opens within the app without redirecting to the App Store app.-

* -Given the App Store review modal is unavailable, fails to load, or is dismissed, when the flow ends, then the app handles the outcome gracefully without blocking login or app usage.-

* -Given the popup has been shown or completed according to the configured display rules, when the same customer logs in again, then the app does not show the popup repeatedly in a disruptive way. (every 90 days the app will ask for the rating again if he has never rate the app)-
* -Given the feature is implemented, when it is tested on supported iOS versions and App Store review configurations, then the rating and review flow behaves consistently and does not introduce login regressions.-

Moving this to Blocked.

While investigating this ticket I traced the call flow end-to-end: {{KazooController::handle()}} ({{app/Http/Controllers/Kazoo/KazooController.php}}) is invoked by Kazoo via {{POST /kazoo/number/handle}}, and it decides {{is_caller_known}} based on {{block_collectors}} and the creditor/blocked-phone tables. On the Kazoo side, the callflow this app provisions per account ({{KazooAPIClient::createCallFlow}}, see the {{is_lawyer_required}} module in {{app/Integrations/KazooAPIClient.php}}) matches a live custom Erlang module I found on the telephony server ({{cf_is_lawyer_required.beam}} on {{logic1}}). I decompiled it and confirmed it only reads a custom channel variable ({{Is-Creditor}}) to decide the branch — it does not call our backend directly.

I need to find where that {{Is-Creditor}} variable actually gets set (i.e., whatever component makes the real HTTP call to {{/kazoo/number/handle}}), since that's outside this repo. I've ruled out FreeSWITCH ({{fs1}}) as the source — no custom Lua/{{mod_xml_curl}}/dialplan curl logic is loaded there, only stock {{mod_kazoo}} — and there's no matching source tree on {{logic1}} either (the {{compile_info}} in the beam file points to {{/usr/local/src/applications/callflow/src/module/cf_is_lawyer_required.erl}}, which doesn't exist on that server).

Based on the CBMA Confluence documentation, the custom Kazoo/Erlang code lives in a separate repository ({{gitlab.velvetech.com/forth-new/cordoba/kazoo}}) that I don't currently have access to. I need access to that repo to locate the actual source for {{cf_is_lawyer_required}} and whatever module sets {{Is-Creditor}}, so I can confirm the real end-to-end flow and safely make changes here without breaking the Kazoo-side integration.

Could someone grant me access, or point me to who owns/maintains that repo?

* Create a user in admin for the person who will perform the password update, so they can verify access still works after the change.
* Change the password.
* Verify the full functionality in Admin.
* Enable MySQL command logs.
